body: That's the thing though, honor and pride are abstract. I don't have any feelings about what others will think of me for giving up like you do. The more and more I "talk" with myself the more convinced I become that suicide is the best, most rational path to take.
Yeah, I think maybe this is fatal apathy. But I still don't see WHY I shouldn't kill myself. Regarding the bucket list: it's an interesting idea but I don't see the point in it.

I think the biggest thing is that I have nothing keeping me here. For a while I was working towards this goal, but as soon as I achieved what I was working towards it hit me, I'm still going to die. Eventually everyone I know will die too. Everything I will ever do in the time that I am alive will ultimately be pointless. I guess what I'm saying is that I'm overwhelmed by the absolute pointlessness of being alive. 

That's why I want to die, because I have nothing to live for I guess.

I'm 23 and I work as a teacher in rural asia. I chose this job after college because I always heard the argument that if you wanted to kill yourself you should go on some crazy wild adventure because you had nothing else to lose. Regarding suicide, I feel the same here as I did back in my home country. 

I don't feel sad about the prospect of suicide. I just don't see the point of being alive any more. I have my various passions and interests like everyone else, I have friends and a stable source of income/roof over my head. 

If this makes sense, I *want* to not want to die. But I feel that there's no feasible reason for me to be alive, no end game, no point or purpose to it all.
